package postgres

// B5 fixture (#87/A1 review): a read exemption must not become a write permit.
//
// This path is deliberately the exact path of a live exemption. hgExempt lists
// (security/infrastructure/postgres/repository.go, audit_events, reads) under
// ADR-0039 D3(d) — the audit append-sink is a cross-cutting platform table and
// a read projection over it was a decided, justified carve-out.
//
// Before B5 the allowlist was keyed by (file, table) alone, so this same file
// could start mutating audit_events and the guard would stay silent: the
// exemption granted for reading covered writing too. The guard's headline claim
// — "a new foreign write is blocked from day one" — was therefore false for
// every exempted file, which is precisely the set of files most likely to reach
// for one.
//
// The fixture proves the fix mechanically, and proves it at the command level:
// the read below must stay silent (the exemption still works) while the write
// must be reported (the exemption does not extend to it).

const auditProjection = `
	SELECT event_id, occurred_at
	FROM audit_events
	WHERE tenant_id = $1
	ORDER BY occurred_at DESC
	LIMIT 50
`

// The same file, the same table, a different verb. No exemption covers this.
const auditBackfill = `
	UPDATE audit_events
	SET redacted = true
	WHERE tenant_id = $1
`
